title: optimize-dashboard-fetch-pipeline-and-harmonize-cache-adapters
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem summary: Several dashboard endpoints are experiencing elevated P95 latencies and memory spikes during peak traffic. Root cause analysis points to a fragmented fetch pipeline: GraphQL resolvers issuing redundant REST/DB calls, multiple cache adapters with incompatible TTL semantics, and an old in-process cache implementation that causes high GC pressure under burst workloads. This ticket refactors the read path to a single aggregation service for dashboard read flows, harmonizes cache adapter behavior across services, and replaces the legacy in-memory adapter with a segmented TTL-aware cache to reduce churn and staleness. Scope: profiler-backed refactor of the dashboard fetch pipeline (server side), adapter interface standardization, upgrade of graphql toolchain to enable resolver-level batching improvements, and integration test + canary rollout. Out of scope: UI changes to dashboard front-end (only backend contract preserved).
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for dashboard_summary and route '/api/console/summary' reduced by >=30% on representative benchmark (current baseline ~420ms -> target <=300ms)
90th percentile memory usage of backend worker processes reduced by >=20% under the same synthetic load
All dashboard read resolvers use the unified cache adapter interface and document TTL semantics
No user-visible regressions (functional tests and smoke tests pass) after canary rollout
Observability: traces show reduced external fanout for unified read path; new metrics exposed: dashboard.fetch.fanout_count and cache.adapter.hit_rate
tasks: Profile current endpoints and capture flamegraphs for 95th percentile requests (benchmark harness)
Author design doc describing unified aggregation service and cache adapter contract (Confluence)
Implement CacheAdapter V2 interface and adapter for segmented TTL cache (replace legacy in-process adapter)
Refactor GraphQL resolvers to call aggregation service instead of firing multiple REST calls
Upgrade graphql-tools to v9 and migrate resolver wiring to leverage new batch helpers
Add integration + load tests to the perf harness and record baseline/after measurements
Create a canary rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error or regression
Update runbook and console docs with new metrics and operational guidance
Deprecate legacy adapter code path and schedule follow-up cleanup
